h1: SEO Company in Guwahati: one office, eight states of demand
metaTitle: SEO Company in Guwahati: All Eight Northeast States
metaDescription: Guwahati firms sell across all eight Northeast states from one address. We build service-area SEO that crosses state lines, on a 90-day baseline guarantee.
answer: A Guwahati business usually serves all eight Northeast states from one address, which the one-city-one-listing model handles badly. The fix is a service-area business profile plus genuinely distinct state-level pages — not rented addresses in Shillong and Imphal. Fake listings get suspended, and the suspension takes your reviews with it.
takeaways: Proximity is a real local ranking factor. Nothing legitimate makes a Guwahati address rank in the Aizawl map pack — so compete in organic results instead, where distance doesn't apply.
A service-area Google Business Profile is the correct setup for distributors and field-service firms. Get it wrong and you lose the listing you already have.
State pages only work if each one contains something the others don't: transit times, local partners, permit rules, actual stock.
English travels furthest across the region — it's the working language of several Northeastern states — but Assamese and Bengali matter enormously within Assam.

sections.h2: Eight states, one address, and a local pack that fights you
body: Guwahati is the region's hub by road, rail and air, which is why so much of the Northeast's distribution, wholesale, healthcare referral and professional services capacity sits here and sells outward. A single office in Guwahati routinely serves Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura and Sikkim.

Google's local results were not designed for that. Google's own documentation describes three factors behind local ranking: relevance, distance and prominence. Distance is measured from the searcher, and it is doing real work — which is why a business in Guwahati does not appear in a map pack for someone searching in Aizawl, roughly 450 kilometres away over mountain roads.

That's the constraint, and it isn't negotiable. What is negotiable is everything above and below the map pack. Organic results have no proximity requirement, and for most of the queries a distributor or B2B service firm cares about, the organic result is where the click happens anyway.

callout.title: The shortcut that ends badly
callout.body: Renting a virtual office in Shillong or Imphal to create a listing there. Google's guidelines require a staffed location at the stated address during stated hours, and suspensions in this category are common. When a profile is suspended you don't just lose the listing — you lose the reviews attached to it, and those took years.

body: If you serve customers at their location rather than yours — distribution, installation, field service, logistics, most B2B — Google's own profile type for you is a service-area business. You hide the street address, keep the location for verification, and declare the areas you serve.

Be clear about what that buys you. It does not project your listing across the region; you'll still surface strongest near your actual location. What it does is stop you looking like a walk-in business that customers can't walk into, remove the address mismatch problems that get profiles flagged, and make the profile consistent with how you actually trade.
Getting it right is mostly discipline rather than skill.
numbered: Pick the service-area setting honestly. Declare the states and districts you genuinely deliver to, not an aspirational map.
Keep NAP consistency across your site, invoices, directories and profile. Inconsistent names and numbers are the most common local ranking drag in the region.
Collect reviews from customers across the states you serve — reviewers' locations add regional signal that no on-page work replicates.
Add the categories you actually operate in, then use products and services fields for the rest. Category is the strongest lever on the profile and the most often left half-filled.
Publish a real contact page: a landline as well as a mobile, working hours in IST, and a WhatsApp route, because a lot of Northeast B2B runs on WhatsApp.
Read the fuller version on [Google Business Profile optimisation](/services/google-business-profile-optimisation).

sections.h2: State pages that aren't the same page eight times
body: Every agency will tell you to build a page per state. Most of them will then build eight pages that differ only in the place name, which is precisely the pattern Google classifies as scaled content abuse — and the penalty lands on the whole domain, not just the thin pages.
A state page earns its URL when it contains information that only applies to that state. In the Northeast that's unusually easy, because the states genuinely differ.

Real differentiators worth building around: transit and delivery times from Guwahati by road, which vary from a half-day to several days; named local partners, dealers or service engineers; whether an Inner Line Permit applies, since Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Mizoram and Manipur require one for visitors from outside; state-specific regulations, licences and registration requirements; local pricing where freight genuinely changes it; and the state's own commercial centres — Dimapur, Silchar, Agartala, Shillong, Imphal, Aizawl, Itanagar, Gangtok — rather than the state name alone.

If you can't write four hundred words of genuinely state-specific detail, build fewer pages. Three strong ones beat eight hollow ones, and the difference isn't cosmetic — it's whether the site gets classified as thin.

sections.h2: Tea: the buyer is in Kolkata, Dubai or Hamburg
body: The Guwahati Tea Auction Centre is one of the largest CTC tea auctions in the world, and Assam's estates supply a global trade. None of that demand is local, and almost none of it is served well online by the people closest to it.

The buyer searching is a blender, importer, private-label brand or wholesale trader. They search in English, by specification: orthodox versus CTC, grade, garden, season and flush, invoice or lot references, organic certification, minimum order quantity. They are not searching for a tea company in Guwahati.

The pages that convert them are a grade-and-garden page rather than a general Products page, a page explaining flush and season with honest cup characteristics, a certification page with real certificate numbers, and a logistics page covering packing, container loading and transit from Kolkata or Haldia. Estates and exporters that publish this outrank the ones with better photography, every time. [SEO for exporters](/seo-for/exporters) covers the wider export-buyer pattern.

There's a second, smaller opportunity most estates ignore entirely: the direct-to-consumer speciality market. People pay considerably more for single-estate tea when there's a story with facts attached — elevation, plucking date, processing. That's a content problem, and it's one the estate is uniquely equipped to solve.

sections.h2: Assamese, Bengali, English — and where each one earns
body: The language decision here is more consequential than in most Indian cities, because the region is genuinely multilingual and the choice determines your reach.

Inside Assam, Assamese is the language of the Brahmaputra valley and Bengali dominates the Barak valley around Silchar. Consumer and local-service searches in Assam lean heavily on both, plus transliterated versions typed on English keyboards, which are frequently different strings from the native-script equivalents and need to be targeted separately.

Across the wider region, English does the heavy lifting. It is the working and official language in several Northeastern states — Nagaland uses it officially, and it's the dominant language of education and administration in Meghalaya, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh. For a Guwahati business selling across state lines, that makes English the practical default for anything regional, with Assamese and Bengali reserved for where they actually convert.

The rule stays the same as everywhere else: write these languages, don't translate into them. Google treats unreviewed machine translation as low-quality content, and a native reader spots it in a sentence. See [English vs regional-language SEO](/compare/english-vs-regional-language-seo) for how to decide the split.

sections.h2: Tourism, where you will not outrank the OTAs head-on
body: Northeast tourism search is dominated by national online travel agencies and large aggregators with domain strength no regional operator will match on generic package terms. Anyone promising you the top spot for a head term like a Kaziranga package is quoting you for a fight they can't win.
The ground you can win is the ground the OTAs can't service: operational specifics that require actually being here.

Permits are the clearest example. Inner Line Permits for Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Mizoram and Manipur are a genuine planning obstacle, the rules change, and the aggregators publish thin, often outdated summaries. A local operator maintaining accurate, dated permit guidance earns both the ranking and the enquiry, because the person reading it has just discovered they need help.

The same logic applies to park season windows — Kaziranga's gates close through the monsoon and reopen for the winter season, and the exact dates move each year — to Ambubachi at Kamakhya, to river conditions on the Brahmaputra, and to road status after landslides. Publish the operational truth, update it with a visible date, and you become the source aggregators quote. Then convert on your own site rather than on someone else's listing. [SEO for travel agencies](/seo-for/travel-agencies) goes further on the direct-booking side.

We don't promise a ranking position, because nobody controls Google's index. We freeze your trailing-90-day qualified leads from organic on day one and guarantee we beat that number in 90 days — otherwise we keep working free until we do.

faqs.q: Can I rank in the map pack across all eight Northeast states from Guwahati?
faqs.a: No, and no legitimate agency can make that happen. Distance from the searcher is one of Google's stated local ranking factors, so a Guwahati address won't surface in an Aizawl map pack. Compete in organic results instead, where proximity doesn't apply, and use a service-area profile for the areas you genuinely cover.

faqs.q: Should I create Google listings in other Northeast cities?
faqs.a: Only where you have a staffed location at that address during your stated hours. Google's guidelines require it, and virtual-office listings in this region get suspended regularly. A suspension takes your reviews with it, which is a far bigger loss than the listing. Use a service-area profile instead.

faqs.q: How many state landing pages should I actually build?
faqs.a: As many as you can fill with genuinely different information — transit times, local partners, permit rules, state regulations, real pricing. If a page only differs by place name, don't publish it. Google classifies near-identical location pages as scaled content abuse and the demotion hits the whole domain.

faqs.q: Do I need Assamese content to rank in Guwahati?
faqs.a: For local consumer and service businesses, Assamese and transliterated Assamese are worth real investment inside the Brahmaputra valley, and Bengali around Silchar. For B2B, export and regional sales across state lines, English reaches further, because it's the working language in several neighbouring states.
